For the Game wizard's 6-step stepper (784px total), the leftmost steps get cut off and unreachable by scroll on mobile since negative overflow can't be scrolled to, and there's no auto-scroll to bring the current step into view. This is a real usability bug I should flag—the fix would be `justify-start sm:justify-center` instead of plain center.

Now I'm working out the mobile layout math: checking the fixed BottomBar's position above the mobile nav bar, the wizard container's bottom padding, and whether the bar's height and positioning actually clear the content correctly given the 844px viewport height.

A bigger concern is the PaymentSlide: on mobile the actual Pay button sits far down the page after payment methods, card panel, and summary sections, but the fixed BottomBar shows a disabled "Next →" button since Next is disabled on the last step. Users could easily see that disabled button and assume they're stuck, never scrolling down to find the real Pay button.

This actually lines up with the data — 23 mobile sessions reached Payment with essentially zero conversions. I also note the card fields only render after a debounced server prepare call, the wallet toggle only appears with a positive balance, and PayPal's SDK only loads when that payment method is selected, so the deck's height measurement via ResizeObserver should still adapt correctly to these conditional elements.

The exit-intent modal is desktop-only since it relies on mouseleave, so mobile users never see that discount offer — not a bug, just a gap. The more interesting issue is the service tile click handler: clicking a highlighted service tile on a deep-linked arrival reseeds the wizard state and wipes out any pre-selected plan or game, which would only affect visitors landing directly on step 0 with a service parameter set.

For game deep-links, arriving with a players param computes the nearest tier by slots, but the game grid is paginated at 21 per page sorted by popularity then alphabetically — so depending on which game they picked, it might not even be visible on the first page, forcing them to page through or accept the reset that comes from clicking the tile again.

Now I'm looking at the funnel drop-off numbers themselves: Game step at 83 sessions, Server at 61, Region at 28, with mobile dropping sharply from 17 to 3. **1. About 33 posts are wider than the phone screen, so the whole page zooms out.**

- **Scope (estimated from the text, not loaded):** about 33 posts, mostly game "set up a dedicated server" guides. The longest token is 71 characters (`/home/palworld/server/Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/PalWorldSettings.ini`). About 31 more are borderline.
- **Fix:** add `min-w-0` to the article (or use `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)]`), and `[overflow-wrap:anywhere]` on the body and on `code`.

**2. Every post shows invented 5-star ratings.**
- `<StarRow rating={5}>` appears three times on every post: the author card (`BlogPostView.tsx:393`) and both product panels (`:511`, next to "Instant deploy · full root · 24/7 support").
- The live HTML carries `aria-label="5 out of 5 stars"` on all 346 posts. This breaks the rule against made-up numbers.
- **Fix:** remove them.

**3. About 28 posts claim a "one-click Mods manager" for games the installer doesn't support.**
- The installer only covers minecraft, rust, valheim, ark, unturned, dst, squad, soulmask, projectzomboid, tf2, l4d2 and empyrion (`lib/mod-install-support.ts:30-56`). Palworld is excluded on purpose.
- Posts still promise it, along with an "EAC toggle" and "drag load order", for Factorio, Enshrouded, V Rising, Satisfactory, tModLoader, 7 Days to Die, Garry's Mod, Conan Exiles and Palworld. Minecraft posts also promise CurseForge/FTB modpack installs, but CurseForge isn't a supported source.
- These include the 12 newest posts (all of `/blog` page 1). Readers who buy on the strength of this will be disappointed.
- **Fix:** rewrite those paragraphs game by game to match what actually works.

**4. On a phone, the first sales link comes very late.**
- The table of contents and its product box are desktop-only (`hidden lg:block`, line 270). The first template call-to-action comes after the whole article (line 367), and the blog has no sticky button.

- **Minecraft:** all 43+ Minecraft posts go to `/game-servers`. None go to `/minecraft-server-hosting` or `/free-minecraft`, and no post links to `/free-minecraft` at all.

<summary>Agent "Audit Nxeon tools pages" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>I audited all 16 tools and made 30 live requests, one at a time. Every tool page returns 200 and every API responds, but there is one Critical issue and four High ones. The Minecraft status page shows fake review ratings and made-up testimonials. The address filter that stops tool APIs reaching internal hosts can be bypassed. The latency test says Nxeon only has Singapore, but Germany is on sale. The size calculator contradicts Nxeon's own plans and prices. And an anonymous visitor who clicks "Register" in the domain generator loses the domain.

Nothing was changed on the server. The POST lookups only touch in-memory rate-limit counters and caches, and write no database rows. The single domain-generator call made one registrar availability check (name.com and Namecheap) and no Claude call. I did not fire the address-filter bypass at production; I proved it with a copy of the filter logic and a local connect.

## Findings, by priority

**1. Critical — fake review scores and invented testimonials on the live `/tools/minecraft-server-status`.**
- **Evidence:** the live HTML shows "4.9 out of 5 on Trustpilot — 312 reviews", "4.8 on HostAdvice — 148" and "4.9 on Google — 205", each twice. The badges link to `#`. The database has 0 rows in `Review` and no `review_url_*` settings, so `ReviewBadges.tsx:29-33` falls back to its demo figures. The demo badges carry no visible label, even though the code comment calls them "clearly-labelled". Testimonials from "mika.exe" and "Jordan P." (`tooltemplate/data.ts:41-44`, rendered at `ToolLanding.tsx:387`) are also live.
- **Why it matters:** this breaches the FTC fake-reviews rule (16 CFR 465) and misuses Trustpilot and Google marks. `ReviewBadges` is shared, so other pages are probably affected too (not checked).
- **Fix:** render nothing when there are no real reviews, and delete `TOOL_REVIEWS`.

**2. High — the internal-address filter lets hex IPv4-mapped IPv6 through.**
- **Evidence:** in `lib/tools/net-guard.ts:57-69`, the mapped-address check only matches the dotted form (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`). `::ffff:7f00:1` passes, as do `::ffff:a14:64` (10.20.0.100) and `::ffff:a9fe:a9fe` (169.254.169.254).
  - `extractHost` keeps these as-is.
  - Locally, `net.connect(22,'::ffff:7f00:1')` connected, with remote `::ffff:127.0.0.1`.
  - The deployed build has the identical logic.
- **Affected routes:**
  - port-checker (`route.ts:51,60-69`) and mc-status (`:189,216`) allow any port.
  - ssl-checker (port 443 only).
  - http-headers is safe only by accident: `URL.hostname` keeps the brackets, which the host check then rejects.
- **Why it matters:** unauthenticated scanning of the hypervisor's localhost (Proxmox on 8006, Postgres, the app itself) and the customer VM network 10.20.0.0/24.
- **Fix:** normalise with ipaddr.js `.process()` and block `::ffff:0:0/96`, `::/96`, `64:ff9b::/96` and `2002::/16`. Also re-check `socket.remoteAddress` after connecting, or add an nftables egress block for the web process.

**3. High — the latency test only measures Singapore and wrongly says Singapore is the only data centre.**
- **What it measures:**
  - The browser makes one discarded warm-up request to same-origin `/api/tools/ping?warmup=1`.
  - It then makes 15 sequential `GET /api/tools/ping?n=i&_=ts` requests with `cache:no-store`, 120 ms apart.
  - Each sample is `performance.now()` from before `fetch` until after `res.arrayBuffer()` (`LatencyTestTool.tsx:42-47`). The warm-up is excluded.
  - The headline is the plain mean, plus best, worst and jitter (mean difference between consecutive samples). There is no median, and it is not a server-side ping.
  - Every request goes to the one origin: nxeon.cloud has a single A record, 51.79.162.96 (OVH Singapore, the primary node), with no CDN and no AAAA record.
  - Each sample includes about 4–5 ms of nginx plus Next.js handling (measured on the box: time to first byte 4.3–4.7 ms on a reused HTTP/2 connection). It does not include TLS, because the connection is reused.
  - It shows no invented numbers for other regions.
- **The problem:** the tool (`LatencyTestTool.tsx:119-129`) and the page's FAQ structured data (`latency-test/page.tsx:28,58-61`) say "we currently serve from a single Singapore data center". In fact node-2 (fsn1, Germany, 178.63.94.114) is enabled and offered in the deploy wizard, and runs 10 customer servers (5 VPS, 5 game).
- **Why it matters:** a European visitor sees 150–250 ms and is told that is what they would get, when Nxeon can host them in Germany.
- **Related, same problem:** the deploy wizard shows every visitor a fixed "~12 ms" for Singapore and "~70 ms" for Germany with signal bars (`lib/nx/catalog.ts:52-62`, `components/nx/OrderBits.tsx:179-182`). A visitor in the US sees "Singapore ~12 ms".
- **Fix:** add a small no-cache endpoint on each region's node, measure one per region with a median, and use the same probe in the wizard.

**4. High — the server size calculator contradicts Nxeon's real products and prices.**
- **Evidence:** it only reads VPS `Plan` rows (`server-size-calculator/page.tsx:37-43`), yet its buttons go to the game, web-hosting and cloud pages. Default outputs, checked against the database:

| Workload (default scale) | Calculator says | What Nxeon actually sells |
|---|---|---|
| Palworld, 8 players | "Exceeds our largest plan — talk to us" | Palworld 8 GB / 8 players at $21.58 |
| ARK: Survival Ascended, 20 players | Exceeds largest plan | ARK:SA 12 GB / 20 players at $38.86 |
| Minecraft, 10 players | Standard, $18.70 | Minecraft 4 GB / 20 slots at $12.94 |
| Rust, 50 slots | Max, $47.50 | Rust 6 GB / 60 slots at $25.90 |
| CS2, 10 players | Pro (8 GB), $30.22 | CS2 tops out at 4 GB / 24 slots, $24.46 |
| Website | "Starter", $12.78 | /web-hosting's "Starter" is $2.99 |

- **Other problems:** "ARK: Survival Ascended" links to `/ark-server-hosting`, which is the Survival Evolved page (`server-sizing.ts:113-122`). The button uses only `productHref` (`ServerSizeCalculatorTool.tsx:108`), with no link to the chosen plan, even though `deployHref({service:"game", gameFamily, players})` / `{planId}` already exists in `lib/deploy-intent.ts`.
- **Fix:** size games against `GamePlan` for that game, web against `HostingPlan`, and link straight to the deploy wizard.

**5. High — an anonymous visitor who clicks "Register" in the domain generator loses the domain.**
- **Evidence:** the link is `/register?domain=…` (`DomainGeneratorTool.tsx:122-125`), but `app/register/page.tsx:36-43` only reads `next` and `error`, and nothing else reads `domain`. The route comment (`route.ts:58-59`) says the name is "carried through"; it isn't. The same bug is in `components/marketing/DomainChecker.tsx:40`.
- **Fix:** `/register?next=${encodeURIComponent('/dashboard/domains/register?domain='+d)}`.

**6. Medium — the "AI Domain Name Generator" has no AI in production.**
- **Evidence:** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is not set in the running `nxeon-web` process, `.env`, or the build's `.env`. The live response had `"source":"heuristic"`. The title, meta text and catalog entry all say "AI" (`domain-generator/page.tsx:7,43`, `catalog.ts:24`).
- **What does work:** it degrades cleanly to the built-in word generator (model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, 20 s timeout) with no errors, but the UI never shows which source produced the names.
- **Fix:** set a funded key, or only say "AI" when `source === "ai"`.

**7. Medium — the domain generator silently ignores every extension after the first two.**
- 12 names × 2 default TLDs = 24, which is exactly `MAX_LOOKUPS` (`domain-suggest.ts:34,37,151-160`; defaults `["com","co"]` in `domain-vocab.ts:193`).
- The live request with com, co and io returned 0 .io results, yet the UI lets you pick up to 6.
- **Fix:** scale the name count to the number of TLDs, or grey out extensions that won't be checked.

**8. Medium — the domain generator can say names are "taken" when they weren't checked.**
- It shows "Every name we tried is already taken" whenever nothing is available (`DomainGeneratorTool.tsx:310-316`), including when every result is "unknown" because the registrar is down or throttled. That contradicts the amber banner just above it.
- A result that is available but has no price is recorded as "taken" (`domain-availability.ts:123-126`).
- **Fix:** base the message on the actual status counts, and map priceless available results to "unknown".

**9. Medium — WHOIS shows the wrong registrar for every .com/.net domain.**
- **Evidence:** the parser's `key.startsWith("registrar")` (`whois/route.ts:67,72`) matches "Registrar WHOIS Server" first. Live github.com showed registrar `whois.markmonitor.com` instead of "MarkMonitor Inc.".
- **Also:** there is no RDAP support (ICANN's standard since January 2025). When IANA gives no referral, IANA's own record is summarised as if it were the domain's.
- **Fix:** match keys exactly; use RDAP with WHOIS as a fallback.

**10. Medium — Minecraft status display problems.**
- MOTDs sent as plain strings keep raw colour codes (`mc-status/route.ts:75`). Live Hypixel shows `§f … §aHypixel Network §c[1.8/26.3]`.
- "Latency" is timed from Singapore and includes the time the server takes to build its status reply (Hypixel: 638 ms), with no "from Singapore" label.
- `Edition: "Java · SRV followed"` is hard-coded (`ToolLanding.tsx:202`), even when no SRV record was followed.

**11. Medium — the /tools hub says "No signup, no limits, no tracking"** (`tools/page.tsx:119`). Every marketing page runs VisitTracker (POST `/api/track`) and the site-wide Meta Pixel, and every API has per-IP limits (for example WHOIS 15/min, domain generator 6/min and 40/hour).

**12. Medium — false feature claims in the related-tools cards** (`tooltemplate/data.ts:18-20`): Port Checker "TCP/UDP" (it only does TCP), DNS "SRV records" (not supported), Latency "Ping our regions" (it pings one).

**13. Low — the latency test fails silently.** `if (!res.ok) continue;` skips both the progress update and the delay. If all 15 requests fail (for example a 429 when many users share one carrier IP; the limit is 240/min per IP), there is no result and no error, and the progress bar freezes. Also: the headline should be a median; the "Nxeon edge" wording is wrong (there is no edge network); the `abort` ref is never set, so there is no cancel.

**14. Low — the "per-target" scan limits never trigger.** In port-checker and mc-status they are keyed by IP plus target at 30/min, which is looser than the per-IP 20/min limit. They do nothing against many IPs scanning one victim; key them on the target alone.

**15. Low — calls to action are generic or overstated.**
- All 15 standard tool pages share one sidebar box linking to `/vps` that promises "a dedicated IPv4" (`ToolShell.tsx:193-203`). Dedicated IP is a $2.99 add-on; 17 of 19 running game servers and 9 of 15 running VPS have none.
- The Minecraft tool's box promises "a dedicated IP" too, and never links to `/free-minecraft`.
- WHOIS, DNS, SSL and HTTP-headers have no link to `/domains` or `/web-hosting`.

**16. Low — rough edges.**
- Every tool calls `res.json()` without a guard, so an nginx HTML error page shows "Unexpected token '<'" (the spinner does stop).
- A null MX record displays as "0\t".
- http-headers rejects URLs with a bracketed IPv6 address.
- The calculator shows the regular USD price, not the intro price or the visitor's display currency.
- The first domain search after a restart took 6.04 s. That equals the 6 s registrar deadline, likely Namecheap's cold pricing cache.
- The domain generator text repeatedly says "our registrar", which clashes with your rule against implying a third-party provider.

**Catalog vs pages:** the 16 catalog slugs match the 16 page folders exactly, all are in the sitemap and all return 200. There are no orphans on either side. `/preview/tool` (not indexed) shows the same fake badges.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

content.thinking:
I notice the free Minecraft server signup also requires email verification, but the marketing copy promises a ready server in about a minute without mentioning that step—so users hit "verify your email first" and have to switch apps to check their inbox, a medium-severity friction point worth flagging. While waiting for that notification, I'll start mentally outlining the report structure, beginning with the deploy wizard funnel section.

Actually, the bigger issue is /free-vps itself: it's the top entry point for signups (351 visits in 30 days, mostly mobile and ChatGPT-referred), driving 61% of sessions to the dashboard and 189 into the deploy wizard, yet it promises a free VPS or free credit that doesn't actually exist anywhere in the product—no signup credit setting, no /dashboard/free-vps route, no matching coupon. The page copy explicitly claims free offers appear in the dashboard and never links to the real free Minecraft tier or the TRIAL798 code, funneling users straight into a paid wizard behind login instead. My fix recommendation: rewrite the page to be honest that there's no free VPS, surface the $2.98 trial and free Minecraft tier instead, and point the hero CTA to registration.

Beyond that, I'm also flagging that the deploy wizard always resets to step 1 even when a marketing CTA pre-selected the plan, term, and game—clicking the highlighted tile re-seeds the order and wipes those selections, and clicking the game tile resets pricing to the cheapest tier, affecting at least 83 deep-link sessions since mid-September. Region selection from marketing links gets silently dropped for game orders too, since only VPS orders apply the passed-in region while the wizard falls back to an unordered default. On top of that, anonymous users clicking the CTA land on a "sign in" page rather than being pushed toward signup.

I'm now cataloguing the many places where registration intent is lost—bare register links, ignored plan/domain query params, the "Already registered" link dropping the next destination—along with a sharp mobile conversion collapse at the payment step, where completion rates are far lower than desktop across both VPS and game orders.

Digging into the code, the culprits stack up: on smaller screens the actual Pay button gets buried below stacked payment method tiles and a tall card panel, while the prominent fixed bottom bar shows a disabled "Next" button since it's stuck at the last step—so the most visible CTA on screen does nothing. There's also leftover desktop copy pointing to card fields "on the left" that's now wrong on mobile, input font sizes small enough to trigger iOS zoom, and no Apple Pay support configured.

Then I flag the pricing contradiction: the site touts price-lock-forever messaging in the hero and FAQ, yet every VPS plan has an intro price that jumps significantly at renewal, and the wizard itself states the renewal price right at checkout—directly undercutting the marketing claim at the worst possible moment, which is a real consumer-protection concern. I'm about to move into the dedicated IP contradictions as the next issue.

These fabricated numbers also feed the marketing GameConfigurator's default "fastest" region selection, steering US/EU buyers toward Singapore unnecessarily.

10. MEDIUM: Email verification only surfaces at the Payment step, blocking with a vague "order can't be taken yet" error instead of catching it earlier in the flow.

This mismatch only surfaces as an amber priceError in the payment summary, and the hostname field itself is buried inside a collapsed Fold, making it easy to miss.

12. MEDIUM (mobile): StepMarks layout with centered justification and horizontal overflow scrolling in OrderBits.tsx...

Also there's an unsourced ETA claim violating the "no invented ETAs" rule, plus a chat bubble overlapping the mobile bottom nav. Looking at the funnel numbers, the biggest drop-offs are people never picking a service (about a third of sessions, especially free-VPS visitors expecting something free), the game server step on mobile, and payment-to-completion. I also notice DeployFunnelEvent never records something important.

For the free tiers, I'm flagging /free-minecraft as critical since it displays fabricated testimonials and a fake average rating, referencing features like a free-to-paid upgrade path that doesn't actually exist.

There's also no real bridge from free to paid: the dashboard lacks any upgrade CTA despite marketing claiming a one-click upgrade that preserves the world, and only 2 of 34 free server owners ever converted. On top of that, the claim button funnels users into a login wall that loses roughly 90% of sessions compared to the VPS flow, and email verification is required but never disclosed on the page.

There's also copy that contradicts the actual product: the site promises "24/7, no queue" and pure vanilla Minecraft, but servers sleep when idle, the backend can only keep about two servers awake simultaneously before refusing new starts, and the real feature set includes multiple game types, mods, and plugin support far beyond vanilla. I'm also noting that /free-vps has no link back to /free-minecraft, and turning to tool-level issues: fake review badges on the server-status tool, an SSRF filter bypass using hex-encoded IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses that can reach internal services, and a latency test that measures from the wrong origin point.

The latency tool only pings a Singapore server through 15 sequential requests, averaging results in a way that includes server processing time and silently skips failures — while marketing claims a "single Singapore data center" even though a German location is also sold to customers, meaning EU users get misleading latency expectations. I'm cataloguing more mismatches too: a size calculator that rejects configurations the catalog actually sells, a domain checker whose "Register" button doesn't work, a domain generator that claims AI but runs on heuristics with broken TLD and availability logic, WHOIS data pointing to the wrong registrar, raw formatting codes leaking into MOTD displays, and a hub page falsely claiming "no tracking, no limits." Finally there are lower-priority issues — generic CTAs pointing to the wrong plans and missing cross-links between tools and hosting pages.

Now shifting to the blog: dozens of posts overflow on mobile due to missing text-wrapping styles, every single post displays a hardcoded 5-star rating regardless of content, and many posts advertise a one-click mod manager for games that aren't actually supported. I'm also noting that the first product CTA appears thousands of pixels down the page on mobile with no sticky fallback, and the generic link-building logic sends most Minecraft and game posts to the wrong product pages instead of their specific hosting plans. There's a long tail of medium and low-severity content issues too — unrendered markdown syntax, duplicate related-post sections, indexable pagination past reasonable limits, missing social preview images, fabricated backdated publish dates, duplicate post pairs, an internal tag leaking publicly, thin "quick answer" boxes that are just excerpts, absent category pages, and unoptimized images without dimensions or lazy-loading.

Moving into mobile-specific findings: the cookie consent banner physically covers the primary CTA on first load across all major landing pages, and there's a z-index conflict where the sticky promo trial bar overlaps the sticky header itself while also wrapping awkwardly on narrow screens — plus a separate stacking conflict where the cookie banner sits at the same z-index as a modal and covers its CTA area on first visit. I'm also flagging that form inputs under 16px font size will trigger iOS Safari's automatic zoom-on-focus behavior on the registration page.

Continuing the mobile audit: /game-servers is loading 141 requests and 6.7MB of unoptimized poster images with 45 broken logo requests, causing 3-4 second load times far above other pages. There's no persistent header CTA on mobile outside the homepage, the pricing page's billing-cycle selector overflows its container hiding the best discount option, the VPS configurator has multiple undersized tap targets, and the web-hosting page has horizontal overflow caused by decorative blur elements extending past the viewport — on top of previously noted wizard and blog overflow issues.

On the "Other" front, I'm flagging a critical issue: fabricated review badges (Trustpilot/HostAdvice/Google ratings) are hardcoded and rendering across roughly 100 pages since the real review table is empty, which violates the FTC's fake reviews rule and likely trademark law — these need to render nothing instead. I'm also noting the homepage falsely claims 7 regions/PoPs with sub-10ms latency when only 2 regions actually exist, contradicting other parts of the site, and that the Meta Pixel is being blocked site-wide by a CSP misconfiguration missing the Facebook connect domain.

Additionally, there's a risky but owner-approved promo popup using fake urgency counters and a fabricated "deployed" toast alongside confirmshaming language, a bloated 619KB homepage HTML payload from RSC flight data and inline SVG, and llms.txt containing false claims about pricing renewal and datacenter location that omit the German infrastructure.

Lower-priority findings: missing Anthropic API key means the chat assistant runs in fallback mode and can't be verified, /web-hosting traffic is dominated by cold-email link scanners inflating analytics, and the contact/newsletter forms appear properly validated with honeypots though untested via actual submission.

Performance looks solid too — TTFB is consistently 80–320ms across key pages. Now I'm waiting on the link agent results before finishing up.

<result>## Nxeon marketing site: CTA and internal-link audit

I checked 1,426 internal URLs against the live site, one request at a time. I also parsed the served HTML of 540 pages: every static marketing page, all 342 live blog posts, 21 NxLabs family pages, 8 sample location pages and the experimental routes. Nothing was edited and no page returned a 5xx. Other than the rows in the table at the end, every link, sitemap URL and anchor I checked works.

### Critical

**1. Made-up review badges on about 700 pages, and they link to `#`**
- **Where:** `components/marketing/ReviewBadges.tsx:29-33`, with the fallback at `:93`. The badges say "4.9 on Trustpilot (312)", "4.8 HostAdvice (148)" and "4.9 Google (205)", each with `href="#"`.
- **Evidence:** They show on 92 of the pages I fetched: the homepage, `/pricing`, `/game-servers` and every game landing page. Every page built on GameLandingCombined (the 615 game×location pages plus the dedicated game pages) shows them too. Every `href="#"` on the site comes from this component.
- **Why it matters:**
  - The code's own comment says these are demo numbers and "Do not publish these figures as genuine". No approved external reviews exist, so the fake set is what's live.
  - Fake review scores are a consumer-protection risk (FTC fake-reviews rule, UK DMCC Act).
  - The links look like they go to review profiles but go nowhere.
- **Fix:** Render nothing when there are no real reviews.

### High

**2. Four Plutonium links 404 and advertise prices for products that don't exist**
- **Where:**
  - Links: `app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx:436-439`.
  - Also listed in `app/sitemap.ts:203-206`.
- **Evidence:**
  - `/plutonium-t4-hosting`, `-t5-`, `-t6-` and `-iw5-hosting` all return 404 live.
  - Each card shows a hardcoded price ($5.99, $6.49, $6.99, $6.79).
  - `/pricing` lists every game with an active plan and has no Plutonium entry. `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts:2126-2129` also records zero Plutonium plan rows.
- **Why it 404s:** No page ever existed at these addresses.
  - There is no `app/(marketing)/plutonium-*` folder.
  - `[slug]/page.tsx` only looks the slug up in four data tables, finds nothing, and calls `notFound()`.
  - Plutonium is left out of `ACTIVE_GAME_FAMILIES` (`gameLocationLandings.ts:277`).
  - The links use a third naming pattern (`-hosting`) that matches neither `GAME_URL_SLUG` (`plutonium-t4-server-hosting`) nor any table.
  - `next.config.ts:185-189` already notes this as a content gap.
- **Fix:** Remove the section and the sitemap entries, or build the pages and seed real plans first.

**3. Game names show as raw internal keys on the main game-server page**
- **Where:** `game-servers/page.tsx:45-65` and the fallback at `:125`. `GAME_META` covers only 19 of the 42 games.
- **Evidence:** In the live `/game-servers` HTML, 23 carousel and configurator cards are titled "abioticfactor", "arkasa", "dst", "l4d2", "kf2", "theisle" and so on. "stationeers" also gets a Deploy button, even though `app/sitemap.ts:181-187` says that server image never starts.
- **Why it matters:** This is the main game-server buying page, and the same bug class has been fixed before (e.g. on `/pricing`).
- **Fix:** Use `GAME_DISPLAY[fam].name` from `lib/games.ts`, and drop stationeers.

**4. "Get your free server" on the server directory is a 404**
- **Where:** `app/(marketing)/game-servers/directory/page.tsx:174` links to `/free-minecraft-hosting`, which returns 404.
- **Why it matters:** It's the main button on a page linked from `/game-servers` and the dashboard nav.
- **Fix:** Point it at `/free-minecraft`.

### Medium

**5. Deploy and claim buttons send new visitors to a "Welcome back" sign-in page**
- **What happens:** Every `deployHref()` link (`lib/deploy-intent.ts:99-113`) points into `/dashboard/*`. For a logged-out visitor that returns a 307 to `/login?next=…`, which shows the heading "Welcome back". The only way to sign up there is a small "Create account" link. The selection is kept, so it isn't broken, but it adds a step.
- **Scale:** 399 deploy links across 72 pages. The same happens with:
  - `/dashboard/free-minecraft`: `freetiertemplate/data.ts:16`, `servers/page.tsx:95,111,155`
  - `/dashboard/migrate`: 11 pages via `migrate/page.tsx` and `MigrateFromPageLayout.tsx:163,270`
  - `/dashboard/hosting`: `WebHostingTemplate.tsx:543,705,838`
  - `/dashboard/claude-code`, `/dashboard/build`
  - Homepage `app/page.tsx:257` links straight to `/login?next=%2Fdashboard%2Fmigrate`.
- **Why it matters:** These are sign-up clicks, and conversion is the known bottleneck.
- **Fix:** Send logged-out deploy traffic to `/register?next=…`. This can be done in the dashboard layout redirect (`app/dashboard/layout.tsx:121`).

**6. CS2 price on `/game-servers` is wrong**
- **Where:** `game-servers/page.tsx:361` hardcodes "CS2 from $6.99/mo".
- **Evidence:** The same live page's own configurator data says $11.99.
- **Fix:** Use the live `fromCents` for every card in that list.

**7. Sitemap contains URLs that don't return a normal page**
- The 4 Plutonium 404s.
- 4 blog posts that redirect (308): `how-to-set-up-a-cs2-server`, `shared-hosting-vs-vps-for-a-growing-site`, `shared-hosting-vs-vps-which-to-choose` and `vps-vs-shared-hosting-which-do-you-need`. They are still marked published in the database.
- The 4 `/legal/*` pages point their canonical tag at the homepage. They inherit `app/layout.tsx:85`.
- **Fix:** Unpublish the 4 duplicate posts, give each legal page its own canonical, and drop the Plutonium entries.

**8. Header menu links are invisible to search engines**
- **Where:** `MarketingHeader.tsx:179,225,261`. The Products menu, Company menu and mobile drawer only render after a click or hover, so none of their links are in the page HTML.
- **Effect:**
  - `/nxcloud` has no crawlable inbound link anywhere. It's not in the footer either.
  - `/nextcloud-hosting` and `/free-vps` each have at most one.
  - The 10 newest game pages (nightingale, squad, space-engineers, kf2, barotrauma, sandstorm, mordhau, the-isle, eco, empyrion) aren't linked from the `/game-servers` hub or the footer. Some of them link to each other.
- **Fix:** Render the menus in the HTML and hide them with CSS, and add these pages to the hub and footer.

**9. `/game-servers` "Explore" link lists are mislabelled**
- **Where:** `game-servers/page.tsx:392-423`.
- **Evidence:**
  - The "no dedicated per-game plan yet — VPS only" heading covers 15 links. 13 of those games (7DTD, Project Zomboid, V Rising, Enshrouded and others) do have live plans on `/pricing`.
  - Line 398 labels the link to `/ark-server-hosting` (ARK: Survival Evolved) as "ARK: Survival Ascended". That duplicates the correct link at line 371.
  - Line 351 still says "Eighteen titles".
- **Fix:** Build these lists from the live plan data.

### Low

- **`/pricing#vps` goes nowhere specific:** It's linked from `compare/page.tsx:192`, but `/pricing` has no such id and no way to deep-link a product tab. Every "Pricing" button on game pages therefore opens the VPS tab: `GameLandingCombined.tsx:830`, `GameConfigurator.tsx:205`, and the related links in `gameLocationLandings.ts:497`. Adding `?product=` support would fix all of them.
- **Affiliate dashboard button:** It points to a bare `/login` (`affiliate/page.tsx:65,160`), so after sign-in people land on the main dashboard instead of the partner area.
- **`www.nxeon.cloud` doesn't redirect:** It returns 200 with the whole site. nginx uses `server_name nxeon.cloud www.nxeon.cloud` and never redirects to the bare domain. Canonical tags limit the SEO damage.
- **Experimental pages:** `/v2`, `/newwebsitev1`–`v8` and all `/preview/*` pages are live (200) but set to noindex (`/v2` without nofollow). None is linked or in the sitemap, so there's no SEO dilution. They do contain their own 404 links (`/deploy`, `/knowledge-base`, `/legal`, `/privacy`, `/terms`), so hiding them in production would be cleaner.
- **`/matrix`** is a real product page (in the header, sitemap priority 0.9), not an experiment.
- **Rate limit on mod pages:** nginx limits `/mods/games/*` to 30 requests per minute per IP. My gentle crawl got 429s at about 4 requests a second, so fast crawlers could be throttled on those pages.
- **Two directory pages:** Two "Public Minecraft server directory" pages compete for the same searches. `/servers` is in the sitemap and footer; `/game-servers/directory` isn't, and its title reads "| Nxeon — Nxeon".
- **External links:** YouTube and Instagram return 200. LinkedIn (999) and Facebook (400) block automated checks, so check them by hand. There is no Discord or external status-page link in the header or footer; "Status" is the internal `/status`, which returns 200.

content.text:
# Nxeon marketing and funnel audit: /free-vps, the deploy wizard, mobile checkout, and fake review badges

The biggest problem is `/free-vps`. It is the top marketing source of signups, but it promises a free VPS or free credit that doesn't exist, so almost nobody who lands there buys. The deploy wizard also loses buyers: it ignores the plan picked on the marketing page and restarts at step 1, and on mobile its payment step almost never ends in a sale. Separately, fake third-party review scores are live on roughly 700 pages.

Nothing was changed on the server. Database access was SELECT-only. Playwright blocked every non-GET request and the ad trackers, so no analytics rows were written. Tools, blog and link checks were run by helper agents; their results are included.

Two things I couldn't see live: the logged-in wizard (it needs an account) and the trial popup (it needs a POST). Those findings come from reading the code. All paths below are under `/opt/nxeon/`.

**What the funnel data shows** (DeployFunnelEvent, since the redesign on 2026-09-14):

| Product | Steps reached | Completed |
|---|---|---|
| VPS | Configure 99 → Region 70 → Payment 58 | 8 |
| Game | Game 83 → Server 61 → Region 28 → Payment 26 | 8 |

- **Mobile vs desktop at payment:**
  - VPS: of those who reached Payment, 7 of 35 desktop sessions completed (20%), but only 1 of 23 mobile (4%).
  - Game Server step on mobile: 17 → Region 3.
- **Where wizard visitors come from:** about 985 wizard sessions in 30 days. Excluding sessions that started inside the dashboard, `/free-vps` is the biggest entry page (189 sessions). The next marketing page, `/free-minecraft`, sends 22.
- **`/free-vps` visitors:** 193 users signed up from it in 30 days, roughly a third of all signups. 2 bought a server and 5 created a free Minecraft server.
- **Tracking gap:** the funnel only starts recording once a service is chosen, so opening the wizard and leaving is never counted.

---

## 1. Deploy wizard and funnel

1. **High: the wizard ignores the marketing selection and opens at step 1.**
   - `const [i, setI] = useState(0)` (`components/nx/DeployView.tsx:1303`). The correct starting step is already worked out in `order.tsx:636` (`activeIdx`) but never used.
   - Deep-linked visitors see "What will you deploy?" with their service highlighted. There were 55 such VPS sessions and 28 game sessions since 09-14.
   - Clicking the highlighted tile calls `chooseService` → `seedOrder` (`order.tsx:163`). That wipes the plan and term they chose (termMonths goes back to 1).
   - For games, clicking the game tile again calls `chooseGame` (`order.tsx:347`), which resets the tier to the cheapest.
   - **Fix:** start at `activeIdx`, or at the first unfinished step, when the URL carries a selection. Make clicking an already-selected tile do nothing.

2. **High: region chosen on marketing pages is dropped for game servers.**
   - `orderFromIntent` only applies `region` when the service is VPS (`order.tsx:281-290`).
   - `GameConfigurator.tsx:141-148` and `GameLandingCombined` (`deployRegion`) both send it anyway.
   - The wizard then defaults to `cat.regions[0]`, which comes from an unordered node query (`app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx:116`). A European visitor who picked Germany gets Singapore.
   - **Fix:** apply the region for games too, and sort the regions.

3. **High: logged-out deploy clicks land on a "Welcome back / Sign in" page.**
   - The redirect is in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx:120-121` and affects 399 deploy links on 72 pages, plus the free-Minecraft, migrate, hosting and build buttons.
   - On a 390px screen the only sign-up route is a 99×20px "Create account" text link. It sits below the fold under the cookie banner, and the chat bubble overlaps the Sign in button (screenshot).
   - Nothing on the page reminds the visitor what they were buying.
   - **Fix:** send logged-out visitors to `/register?next=…` and repeat the chosen product there.

4. **High: many buttons lose what the visitor chose.**
   - 58 buttons link to plain `/register`, which drops the visitor on `/dashboard` after sign-up. These include the homepage hero, `StickyCTA`, `VpsConfigurator.tsx:170` and the Register/Transfer buttons in domain search results (`DomainsLanding.tsx:347,357`).
   - `/register?plan=` (`RocketPricing.tsx:82`) and `/register?domain=` (`DomainChecker.tsx:40`, `DomainGeneratorTool.tsx:125`) are ignored, because `app/register/page.tsx:36-43` only reads `next`.
   - "Already registered? Log in" drops `next` (`components/AuthForms.tsx:379`).
   - **Fix:** carry every selection through `next`.

5. **High: the mobile payment step, where mobile buyers disappear (4% vs 20%).** Causes found in the code:
   - On screens narrower than `lg`, the Pay button is at the bottom of the order summary. Above it are three stacked payment-method tiles and a card panel at least 280px tall (`DeployView.tsx:725,756,1146`).
   - Meanwhile the fixed bottom bar shows a greyed-out "Next →" (`disabled={... i >= last}`, `:466`). The most visible button on the screen does nothing.
   - The text "Card details on the left." (`:1057`) is wrong on mobile, where the card fields are above.
   - The "why Next is blocked" hint is hidden on mobile (`hidden … sm:block`, `:461`).
   - Wizard inputs are 13px, so iOS zooms in when a field is tapped.
   - Apple Pay can't appear: `/.well-known/apple-developer-merchantid-domain-association` returns 404. Worth confirming in the Stripe dashboard.
   - **Fix:** on the payment step, make the bottom-bar button the Pay button (or scroll to it); fix the copy; show the hint; use 16px inputs; register the Apple Pay domain.

6. **High: `/pricing` says prices never rise at renewal, but checkout shows a 44% increase.**
   - The page says "The price you sign up at is the price you renew at — it never increases at renewal" (`PricingExplorer.tsx:252,465`). The pricing FAQ (`pricing/page.tsx:54`) and `llms.txt` say the same.
   - All 4 VPS plans have intro prices. Starter is $8.88, then $12.78.
   - The payment summary says "Renews at $12.78/mo after your first month" (`DeployView.tsx:1026-1029`). The contradiction appears exactly when the customer is about to pay.
   - This is a consumer-protection risk. **Fix:** change the claim.

7. **High: "dedicated IPv4" is advertised as included but sold as an extra, and IPv6 doesn't exist.**
   - 56 marketing files say "dedicated IPv4" is included. `/vps` shows "IPv4 + IPv6" (`vpstemplate/VpsLanding.tsx:223`, `data.ts:136`).
   - The wizard sells a $2.99/mo "Dedicated IP" add-on for VPS (`deploy/page.tsx:318`). The worker already gives VPS a dedicated IP for free by default (`worker/index.ts:766-769`, `dedicated_ip_default=true`), so customers can pay for something they would get anyway.
   - When the IP pool is empty it quietly falls back to NAT. 7 of 13 running paid VPS have no dedicated IP, and 0 servers have IPv6.
   - **Fix:** make the copy and the checkout say the same thing.

8. **Medium: fixed latency figures shown as if measured.**
   - The region cards show "~12 ms" for Singapore and "~70 ms" for Germany to every visitor (`lib/nx/catalog.ts:53-63`, `OrderBits.tsx:179-182`, order summary `DeployView.tsx:936`).
   - The marketing configurator picks the "fastest" default region using those same numbers.
   - This steers US and EU buyers to Singapore. **Fix:** measure it in the visitor's browser, or remove the numbers.

9. **Medium: the email-verification requirement only shows up at Payment, as a dead end.**
   - The panel says "This order can't be taken yet". Its "Change the order" button goes back to Configure, which doesn't help. There is no inline resend button.
   - The error never clears after the customer verifies (`DeployView.tsx:584-617`) unless they change the order.
   - The verification page links to `/dashboard` (`app/verify-email/page.tsx:100`), not back to the order.
   - 15–20% of recent signups are unverified.
   - Free Minecraft has the same requirement (`lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`), and the marketing page never mentions it.

10. **Medium: hostname rules differ between the browser and the server.**
    - The browser accepts 2 or more characters of anything (`order.tsx:602`). The server requires 3–40 letters, digits or hyphens (`lib/order.ts:86-90`).
    - The error only appears as an amber price error at Payment, while the hostname field sits inside a collapsed section.

11. **Low:**
    - The step indicator uses `justify-center` inside a scrolling row (`OrderBits.tsx:256-263`). With 5–6 steps (648–784px), the left-hand steps are cut off and can't be scrolled to on mobile.
    - Term and genre chips are clipped with a hidden scrollbar.
    - The "Cancel" button on step 0 is permanently disabled (`DeployView.tsx:403-406`).
    - A "Crypto — Not enabled" tile is shown at payment.
    - "Answers in about four minutes" (`DeployView.tsx:182`) is an unsourced support-time claim.
    - In the portal on mobile, the chat bubble covers the bottom nav bar (`ChatWidget.tsx:1170`, no dashboard offset).

## 2. Free tiers

1. **Critical: `/free-vps` promises something that doesn't exist.**
   - The page says free-credit and free-VPS offers "show up right in your dashboard" and "Your server simply pauses or you're prompted to add payment".
   - In reality there is no signup credit, `/dashboard/free-vps` returns 404, and no free-VPS coupon exists. The hero "Deploy now" button leads to a paid wizard behind the login page.
   - There is no link to `/free-minecraft`, the one real free product, or to the $2.98 TRIAL798 trial.
   - Evidence: 351 entries in 30 days (52% mobile, 37% from ChatGPT); 61% of those sessions reach the dashboard; 193 users → 2 buyers.
   - **Fix:** say plainly that there's no free VPS; lead with the trial and free Minecraft; add the same line to `llms.txt` so ChatGPT stops recommending a "free VPS".

2. **Critical: `/free-minecraft` shows invented testimonials and a made-up rating.**
   - The page renders `REVIEWS`: "leo_builds · Free tier · 6 months", although the tier launched on 2026-08-24. It also shows "RedstoneRex: upgraded… one click. Kept our world" and "4.9 from free-tier players".
   - These come from `freetiertemplate/data.ts`, whose own header says "PREVIEW-ONLY… ILLUSTRATIVE". The fake review badges also appear.

3. **High: there is no bridge from free to paid.**
   - The free Minecraft dashboard has no upgrade button (`FreeMcDashboard.tsx:63` says "no tier upgrade"), and nothing moves a world to a paid server.
   - The page claims "Upgrading is one click… keeps your world".
   - 34 free servers exist; 2 of their owners have ever bought anything.
   - **Fix:** add an "Always-on upgrade" button that deep-links to the Minecraft deploy, plus a world import.

4. **High: "Claim your free server" goes to the sign-in wall** (`data.ts:16`). Only 9% of desktop and 6% of mobile `/free-minecraft` sessions reach the dashboard, against 56–66% for `/free-vps`.

5. **Medium: the page contradicts itself and the product.**
   - The headline says "24/7", but the server sleeps when idle.
   - The FAQ (also in the FAQPage structured data that LLMs read) says "runs vanilla Minecraft" 4 times. The comparison table says "Presets + core plugins", and the product actually has 9 game types, a mods menu and a permissions plugin.
   - "No queue" is not accurate: the host can run only about 2 servers awake at once (`lib/freemc-capacity.ts` header).

## 3. Tools

- **Critical:** `/tools/minecraft-server-status` shows the fake review badges plus invented testimonials (`tooltemplate/data.ts:41-44`, rendered at `ToolLanding.tsx:387`).
- **High (security):** the filter that stops tool APIs reaching internal hosts can be bypassed with hex IPv4-mapped IPv6, e.g. `::ffff:7f00:1` for 127.0.0.1 (`lib/tools/net-guard.ts:57-69`).
  - This affects port-checker (any port), mc-status and ssl-checker. It could reach localhost, Proxmox on 8006, and the customer VM network 10.20.0.0/24.
  - This was proven locally and not fired at production.
  - **Fix:** normalise addresses with ipaddr.js `.process()`, block the mapped and translation ranges (`::ffff:0:0/96`, `::/96`, `64:ff9b::/96`, `2002::/16`), and re-check the socket's remote address after connecting.
- **High: what `/tools/latency-test` measures today.**
  - The browser makes one warm-up request (discarded), then 15 sequential `GET /api/tools/ping` requests with `cache:no-store`, 120ms apart.
  - Each sample is `performance.now()` around `fetch` plus `arrayBuffer`. The headline is a mean (not a median), plus best, worst and jitter.
  - Every request goes to one origin, 51.79.162.96 in Singapore. Each sample includes about 4–5ms of server processing. TLS is not included because the connection is reused. It is not a server-side ping.
  - The tool and its FAQ structured data say "single Singapore data center", which is false: the Germany region is on sale and runs 10 customer servers. A European visitor is told to expect 150–250ms.
  - It fails silently: `if (!res.ok) continue;` means that if every request fails, the progress bar just freezes. There is also no cancel.
- **High:** the size calculator only looks at VPS plans.
  - For Palworld with 8 players it says "exceeds our largest plan", but an 8GB Palworld plan is sold at $21.58. For a website it suggests a $12.78 VPS instead of $2.99 hosting.
  - It never links to a specific plan.
- **High:** the domain generator and domain checker "Register" buttons drop the domain.
- **Medium:**
  - The "AI" domain generator has no API key set (it returns `source=heuristic`), and extensions after the second one are ignored.
  - "Taken" is shown for names that weren't actually checked.
  - WHOIS shows the wrong registrar for .com and .net.
  - Minecraft MOTDs show raw `§` colour codes.
  - The `/tools` hub says "no tracking, no limits", but both exist.
- **Low:** every tool's sidebar links to `/vps` and promises "a dedicated IPv4". The Minecraft tool doesn't link to `/free-minecraft`.

## 4. Blog (346 posts)

- **High:**
  - About 33 posts are wider than a phone screen (scrollWidth 615 at 390). The article has no `min-w-0` (`BlogPostView.tsx:267/319`), and code has no `overflow-wrap` (`lib/blog.ts:213`).
  - `StarRow rating={5}` shows made-up ratings on every post (`BlogPostView.tsx:393,511`).
  - About 28 posts promise a one-click mods manager for games the installer doesn't support.
  - On mobile, the first sales link is about 5,700px down the page, with no sticky CTA.
  - `productLinkForPost` (`lib/blog.ts:123-158`) is generic: 43 Minecraft posts go to `/game-servers` and never to `/free-minecraft`; 6 game guides go to `/vps`.
- **Medium:**
  - Raw markdown shows on the page: `*italics*` in 138 posts, tables rendered as pipes in 4.
  - "Related guides" is the same for every post in a category.
  - `?page=9999` is an indexable duplicate.
  - 146 posts have no social-share image.
  - 104 posts show publish dates earlier than the blog existed.
  - There are 11 pairs of near-duplicate posts, and the internal `#seobatch` tag is visible.
- **Checked and fine:** all 274 internal link targets inside posts work, and the sitemap matches the database.

## 5. Broken links and CTAs

- **Confirmed 404s:**
  - `/plutonium-t4-hosting`, `-t5-`, `-t6-`, `-iw5-` are linked from `app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx:436-439`, listed in `app/sitemap.ts:203-206`, and shown with hardcoded prices. No route or plan exists for them.
  - `/free-minecraft-hosting` is the main button on `/game-servers/directory` (`directory/page.tsx:174`).
- **High:** 23 game names on `/game-servers` show as raw internal keys, e.g. "abioticfactor", "l4d2" (`page.tsx:45-65,125`). "stationeers" gets a Deploy button although its image never starts.
- **Medium:**
  - CS2 is hardcoded at "$6.99" when the live price is $11.99 (`page.tsx:361`).
  - The "VPS only" heading covers 13 games that do have plans (`:392-423`).
  - The sitemap lists 4 blog posts that 308-redirect.
  - The `/legal/*` pages point their canonical at the homepage.
  - The header menus only render after a click or hover, so `/nxcloud` and the 10 newest game pages have no crawlable inbound links.
- **Low:**
  - `/pricing#vps` doesn't exist, so every "Pricing" button on game pages opens the VPS tab.
  - `www.nxeon.cloud` serves the whole site instead of redirecting.
  - `/newwebsitev1`–`v8`, `/v2` and `/preview/*` are public (noindex) and contain their own 404 links.

## 6. Mobile (390×844)

Page-level horizontal overflow: none on 20 of the 21 key pages measured. `/web-hosting` scrolls sideways by 12px because of decorative glows.

1. **High: the cookie banner hides the primary CTA on first visit.** It takes 199px of the 844px screen at z-70 (`CookieConsent.tsx:64`) on `/free-vps`, `/free-minecraft`, `/pricing`, `/game-servers` and `/login`. Consent is opt-out anyway, so a slim bar would do.
2. **High (from the code, not seen live):** the trial promo bar is `position:sticky; top:0; z-index:55` and is rendered before the header (sticky, top-0, z-50). While scrolling it sits over the logo and menu button, and it wraps to several lines at 390px (`globals.css:2982`, `(marketing)/layout.tsx:22`). The promo modal and the cookie banner are both z-70, and the banner is later in the page, so it covers the bottom of the modal where the CTA is.
3. **High:** input font sizes are below 16px on `/register` and `/login` (14px), `/contact`, and all wizard fields (13px), so iOS zooms in on tap.
4. **High: `/game-servers` is heavy on mobile.**
   - 141 requests and about 6.7MB of images: roughly 460KB raw JPG posters, not served through next/image.
   - 45 404s, from 23 missing game logos with an SVG-then-PNG fallback each.
   - Load time 3.3–4.1s, versus 0.3–0.6s for other pages.
5. **Medium:**
   - There is no CTA in the mobile header; "Get started" is only inside the drawer (`MarketingHeader.tsx:206`).
   - The `/pricing` billing selector is 538px wide inside a 390px scroller, so "Triennial −40%" (the best deal) is off-screen.
   - On the `/vps` slider, the tick targets are 14×17px and the track is 8px tall.
   - The review-badge links are 30px tall and go to `#`, and the carousel dots are 6×6px.

## 7. Other

1. **Critical: fake third-party review badges site-wide.** `ReviewBadges` falls back to `DEMO_BADGES` ("4.9 Trustpilot (312) / 4.8 HostAdvice (148) / 4.9 Google (205)", linking to `#`) because the `Review` table has 0 rows (`ReviewBadges.tsx:29-33,93`). They are unlabelled and appear on about 700 pages. This is exposure under the FTC fake-reviews rule, plus misuse of the Trustpilot and Google marks. **Fix:** render nothing.
2. **High:** the homepage `NetworkMap` claims "7 regions · <10 ms metro latency" with points of presence in Toronto, New York, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Tokyo and Sydney (`NetworkMap.tsx:37-41,61`). Only Singapore and Germany exist.
3. **High:** the Meta Pixel is blocked by the site's own Content Security Policy on every page. `next.config.ts:25` `script-src` doesn't include `https://connect.facebook.net`, and the browser console shows the violation. Only server-side conversion events reach Meta.
4. **Medium:** the trial popup's "Only X spots left" counter goes down on a timer and shows a fake "Server deployed ✓" toast (`PromoTrialPopup.tsx:48-50,97-113`). It also says "free trial" while charging $2.98. These are documented owner choices, flagged here only as a compliance risk.
5. **Medium:** the homepage HTML is 619KB (141KB compressed). About 354KB of that is React Server Components data and 101KB is the inline network-map SVG. A single 426KB stylesheet (60KB compressed) loads on every marketing page. Server response times are fine (80–320ms).
6. **Medium:** `llms.txt` repeats the "renews at the same price" and "Singapore-only" claims, and says nothing about the free VPS.
7. **Low:**
   - There is no Anthropic API key in `.env` or settings, so the AI chat and domain generator run in fallback mode.
   - 75% of `/web-hosting` entries are cold-email clicks averaging 19 seconds, likely link scanners.
   - The contact and newsletter forms have server actions, required fields, length limits and a honeypot; I didn't submit them.

Screenshots, scripts and the helper agents' working files are in `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/mkt/` (the `shots`, `blog`, `tools` and `links` folders).
